article.contentMarkdown:
# How Ganesh Chaturthi Is Celebrated in Maharashtra, Day by Day

Ganesh Chaturthi is celebrated in Maharashtra as a ten-day house guest rather than a single festival day: the murti arrives on Chaturthi, is worshipped and fed twice daily, is joined mid-festival by the goddess Gauri, and is immersed on Anant Chaturdashi. In 2026 that arc runs Monday 14 September to Friday 25 September in Mumbai — twelve calendar dates, not ten, because the Chaturthi and Chaturdashi tithis do not fall a neat ten days apart. Households immerse on the first, third, fifth, seventh or last day by family custom, and three Jyeshtha Gauri days sit inside the arc on 17, 18 and 19 September. Everything below is dated. The platform figures are SubhSandesh's own: 3,894 personalised pages created since 2026-03-12, across 15 page types, and 49.6% of shared pages opened on a phone, 22,817 of 46,005 views.

## What Ganeshotsav in Maharashtra actually is

Ganeshotsav is the Maharashtrian form of Ganesh Chaturthi: a domestic installation of Ganesha that runs for a set number of days, held alongside a public one organised by neighbourhood mandals. The two calendars overlap but are not the same calendar, and confusing them is why most explainers of this festival read as vague. A household observance can be over by the second afternoon while the mandal two lanes away runs the full eleven days.

The public half is a modern layer on an old household rite. The Urban History Association's *The Metropole* dates the shift to 1893, when Bal Gangadhar Tilak pushed public celebration in Bombay and Pune, and [names the Keshavji Naik Chawl mandal in Girgaum, established that same year](https://themetropole.blog/2026/06/26/playing-the-city-ganesh-utsav-and-the-politics-of-urban-public-space/), as one of the earliest examples. The household rite is older and has no founding date.

## The 2026 Maharashtra Ganeshotsav calendar, day by day

Six dated points define the arc in Mumbai this year. Every household sits somewhere on this list depending on how long it keeps the murti, and no household does all six — you install once, you immerse once, and the Gauri days either fall inside your window or after it has closed.

### 1. Monday 14 September — aagman and sthapana

The murti is fetched home in a small procession, seated on a decorated chaukat or mandap, and given pranapratishtha at the Madhyahna muhurat, 11:20 AM to 01:48 PM for Mumbai. Modak and durva are offered, and the first aarti is sung that evening. Everything after this day is repetition of the morning and evening aarti, with variations only at the exit.

### 2. Tuesday 15 September — the dedh-din visarjan

The shortest common observance is a day and a half: install on the 14th, immerse on the afternoon of the 15th. This is the working household's choice and it is not a lesser observance, only a shorter one. Uttar puja is performed before the murti is lifted.

### 3. Wednesday 16 September — the third-day immersion

Families keeping Ganpati for three days immerse on the 16th. From here the daily pattern is fixed: two aartis, naivedya at midday, and visitors through the evening. The mandal pandals nearby are running their own programme on a louder schedule.

### 4. Thursday 17 to Saturday 19 September — the three Gauri days

Jyeshtha Gauri arrives on the 17th, is worshipped on the 18th and takes leave on the 19th. This is the part of the arc that no competing calendar prints, and it changes what a household is doing on days four through six entirely. Detail in the next section.

### 5. Sunday 20 September — the seventh-day immersion

Seven-day households immerse on the 20th, after the Gauri have already gone. This is the most common compromise for families who want the full mid-festival stretch without holding the murti to the end.

### 6. Friday 25 September — Anant Chaturdashi

Anant Chaturdashi falls on Friday 25 September 2026 in Mumbai, with the Chaturdashi tithi running from 11:18 PM on 24 September to 11:06 PM on 25 September. This is when the large mandals immerse, and when the processions that close Bhadrapada shukla take the streets.

## Jyeshtha Gauri: the three days no calendar prints

Jyeshtha Gauri is a three-day observance for Gauri, a form of Parvati, nested inside Ganeshotsav and specific to Marathi households. Drik Panchang places [Gauri Avahana on Thursday 17 September 2026 with a muhurat of 06:26 AM to 06:39 PM](https://www.drikpanchang.com/marathi/festivals/gauri-puja/jyeshtha-gauri-avahana-date-time.html?year=2026&geoname-id=1275339) for Mumbai, Gauri Puja on the 18th and Gauri Visarjan on the 19th.

Two things about it are worth knowing before you plan around it. First, the symbolism is a married daughter arriving from her maternal home, which is why the reception is a household one led by the women of the house and why Gauri is offered the sixteen adornments of a married woman. Second, this visarjan is not an immersion — it is a ceremonial farewell, and the metal, stone or wooden Gauri are usually kept.

Many families in coastal Maharashtra bring two, Jyeshtha Gauri paired with Kanishtha Gauri, worshipped as Mahalakshmi. If your household immerses Ganpati on the fifth or seventh day, the Gauri days land on top of the exit, and in practice both farewells get combined.

## How long the murti stays, and what that costs you in notice

If you are sending a greeting rather than attending, the arc is a deadline problem. The last column is SubhSandesh's own lead-time measurement, and it is a sobering one.

| Observance | 2026 date, Mumbai | Notice from 10 September | Rakhi pages built with that much notice, n = 89 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ganpati sthapana | Mon 14 Sep | 4 days | 6.7% |
| Dedh-din visarjan | Tue 15 Sep | 5 days | 6.7% |
| Jyeshtha Gauri avahana | Thu 17 Sep | 7 days | 6.7%, and 7 days was the earliest recorded |
| Gauri visarjan | Sat 19 Sep | 9 days | 0% |
| Anant Chaturdashi | Fri 25 Sep | 15 days | 0% |

Two disclosures that matter, because the measurement is not of this festival. It measures **Raksha Bandhan 2026, not Ganesh Chaturthi** — a one-day festival against Ganeshotsav's ten, which is exactly the difference this post is about. And **n = 89 is small**, so no per-template, per-region or per-language rate can be drawn from it; the honest reading is a shape, not a rate.

Across those 89 pages, 49.4% were built on the festival day itself and the median lead time was 0 days. There is no Ganesh Chaturthi equivalent to compare it against: the [Ganesh Chaturthi page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) went live on 2026-09-10, four days before the festival, so no page-creation data for it exists at all yet.

## The Konkan version is not the Mumbai version

Regional practice inside Maharashtra varies more than the tourism copy admits. In Rajapur tehsil in Ratnagiri, the canopy above the murti is a *matvi* — a wooden frame ceremonially dressed with seasonal wildflowers gathered from the surrounding landscape. A 2023 survey across [eight villages in Rajapur documented the plant species used and warned that the tradition is changing](https://doi.org/10.54081/jes.028/03), which is a real finding about a real practice and not a decorating tip.

Urban Ganeshotsav pulls the other way, outward into the street. A peer-reviewed study of Mumbai reads the festival as [a ten-day transformation that encapsulates the whole city](https://doi.org/10.1515/culture-2019-0009), turning a financial capital into a layered carnival ground. Noise monitoring at Mumbai community pandals in 2020, [compared against 2018 and 2019](https://doi.org/10.1515/noise-2021-0006), found levels fell sharply in the pandemic year — a measured reminder that the loudness of the public festival is a choice, not a fixture.

## Sending Ganeshotsav to someone who is not in Maharashtra

The arc is the problem: a relative in Dubai or Bengaluru misses a ten-day rhythm, not one afternoon. A page they open on their own phone at least gives them something to do rather than watch — 49.6% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, and 96.0% of started pages actually get published and shared, 3,737 of 3,894.

The Ganesh page is built to be performed by the recipient: they offer the durva, kumkum, flowers and modak themselves, the aarti thali circles, and they write a prarthana back. If you want to see what you are committing to before you start, the [written build guide for the Ganesh Chaturthi page](https://subhsandesh.in/guides/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) walks through it step by step. The same mechanism exists for other festivals — the [Raksha Bandhan page for a brother](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-brother) is where the lead-time numbers above came from.

## When a SubhSandesh page is the wrong choice

Three cases, plainly. If the person is in the same room, send nothing and hand them a modak. If they have no smartphone, a page fails outright: half our views are phone views and a desktop-only recipient gets a worse version of the same thing.

And if what they actually want is the Gauri reception or the visarjan procession, a link is not a substitute for being there — it is an acknowledgement that you are not. Occasion-dated pages, every festival plus every wedding type, are only 144 of 3,894 pages, 3.7%; the platform is 96.3% romantic and everyday pages, which is worth knowing before assuming this is what we are built for.

## Watch the page get built

Ninety seconds, start to finish — the aarti going round, the five offerings, and the box at the end where they write a line back to you: [Ganesh Chaturthi Wishes Online — Full Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpWiv5T59QY). More page walkthroughs on Instagram: [@subhsandesh_official](https://www.instagram.com/subhsandesh_official).

## Sources

- *Journal of Ecological Society* — "Matvi: An Eco-Cultural Tradition of Wildflower Decoration from Rajapur Tehsil, Ratnagiri Dist., Maharashtra, India", 1 April 2023 (CC BY; abstract read).
- *Open Cultural Studies* — "Heterotopic Assemblages within Religious Structures: Ganesh Utsav and the Streets of Mumbai", 1 February 2019 (CC BY; abstract read).
- *Noise Mapping* — "Effects of COVID-19 pandemic on festival celebrations and noise pollution levels", 2021 (CC BY; abstract read).
- Drik Panchang — Jyeshtha Gauri Avahana 2026 date and muhurat for Mumbai (date and festival reference).

auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page on this SERP that prints a date for anything: all five analysed competitors say "ten days" and then describe day one and the last day, four of them undated and one year-stamped 2020, and none of them places the three Jyeshtha Gauri days on a calendar at all. That plus the correction that Gauri visarjan is a farewell rather than an immersion, and the arithmetic that the ten-day festival spans twelve calendar dates in 2026, is a genuine retrieval position an answer engine has reason to prefer. The weaknesses are real: the metaTitle differentiator ("Dated") is thin, three of the five citations rest on publisher abstracts rather than full texts, and the first-party lead-time evidence measures Raksha Bandhan at n = 89 rather than this festival, which the body says twice. Domain authority sits far below two state tourism boards and Prasar Bharati on this SERP, so any movement is a matter of months and is not predicted here.
